Distribution. Drâa-Tafilalet region in southern Morocco. Pollen hosts. Three pollen samples from two different localities exclusively contained pollen of Convolvulaceae (Tab. 1), suggesting a distinct or possibly even exclusive preference for this plant family. Distribution (Fig. 62). Pierella chalybaea is distributed in Brazilian and Chacoan sub-regions, from Colombia to Bolivia (Constantino 1995; Willmott et al 2011; Willmott & Hall 2014; Petit 2014) and North and Midwest Brazil (Roraima, Amazonas, Pará, Acre, Rondônia, Mato Grosso and Goiás), apparently associated with both low altitudinal regions (100 – 900 m) (Brown 1948) and high rainfall levels between 2000 – 5000 mm / year (Brown & Ab’Saber 1979). Host plant. Unknown.

Distribution (Figs. 1, 26): Leonesiella tetratriches sp. nov. is only known from MSS from two sites 1 km apart, on the slopes of a hill in Salientes bordered to the west by the Prao Viejo stream basin and to the south by the Valseco River. Although this area is located in the southern foothills of the Cantabrian Mountains, it is somewhat isolated from them by the Sil and Luna river basins. To the southeast, this area is bordered by the Tertiary basin of the Duero, in which no species of Leptodirini is known to occur, while to the west it borders an area where numerous localities of L. bergidi are known. This species is the westernmost of all species of the genera in the Quaestus group. Its range extends along the western foothills of the Montes Aquilanos and the Sierra de la Lastra in the province of León, the Sierras de Avellaneira and la Lastra in the province of Orense, the Sierras del Caurel and de Ancares in the province of Lugo, and the Sierra del Rañadoiro and Montes de Muniellos in the province of Asturias (Fresneda & Salgado 2017). The caves are located in a discontinuous karst clearly isolated from the Cantabrian limestones, which are mainly composed of the so-called " Aquiana and Vegadeo limestones ", in which the cavities show an obvious fossilisation process. This species has also been recorded in MSS (Salgado et al. 2008). It should be noted that the new species is present in an area with siliceous substrate.
